title: Split scripts/lib/common.sh under the 250-line cap
objective: Bring the shared library that 49 scripts source under the cap, without changing any name it exports or requiring a single consumer to be edited.
acceptance_criteria: common.sh and all three new parts are at most 250 lines.
common.sh remains the single path every consumer sources; it sources its own parts, so no caller changes.

Sourcing common.sh yields exactly the same set of function names as before the split, proven by diffing `declare -F` against a detached worktree at HEAD. A passing lint is not sufficient evidence for a library with this many consumers.
Any array or constant a moved function reads moves with it, rather than being left behind and suppressed.
The pre-commit shellcheck hook passes on every file, with no new suppression.
The parts are sourced in the original definition order, so a consumer relying on ordering is unaffected.
out_of_scope: Executing any of the 49 consumer scripts.
verifier: A subshell that sources common.sh and prints `declare -F`, diffed against the same run from a detached worktree at HEAD; plus array-length checks, shellcheck -x, meta/scripts/verify_shell_split.sh on a real consumer, and check_file_length.sh.
